User-provided rubric: user_analytical_writing_1_to_4_v1
Thesis: Responds to prompt with specificity; is arguable and insightful; contains an interesting "so what" or makes space for a concluding "so what?"
Evidence: Allows for inference and discussion of language; aligns with your argument and moves it forward; represents logical and rich selection that sufficiently supports the thesis
Organization: Introduction and conclusion provide a frame for the argument; has clear and focused topic sentences and sub-arguments that support and develop the idea presented in the thesis; uses effective transitions between ideas and paragraphs; uses concluding sentences that effectively pull the paragraph together; shows deliberate organization of paragraphs and evidence within paragraphs
Analysis: Supports and/or advances the argument; features intentional examination of language and techniques; offers valid and insightful interpretation; avoids plot summary, paraphrasing, and repetition
Control of language: Establishes appropriate academic voice; uses precise word choice and varied sentence types; contextualizes and elegantly incorporates quotations
Mechanics/conventions: Avoids spelling, punctuation, and grammatical errors; formats MLA/parenthetical correctly; avoids mechanical errors
